cards.front: Patient with diagnosed CMT performs a coleman block test . Results are shown below. Which procedures (2) would correct this deformity? Tibialis posterior tendon transfer Dorsiflexion osteotomy of first ray
cards.extra: This is an example of a Coleman block test that corrects... If it corrects, this suggests a forefoot driven varus. Likely secondary to peroneus longus overpowering a weak tibialis anterior. If it does not correct, this suggests hindfoot driven varus. Likely secondary to hindfoot arthritis. This would need to be treated with a triple arthrodesis. Guyton et al. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11232233/) review the surgical management of foot deformities in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. They note that deformities are variable between patients and care should be individualized. They recommend addressing the plantar fascia first then proceeding from the hindfoot to the forefoot during the correction, as a hindfoot procedure may alter the resting tension of the digital flexors and extensors.
